## Comparability caveat

Four of the five carriers report clean, full calendar-year 2024 results [DOC-1]. **Alaska is not directly comparable**: it closed the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869M of revenue and a $113M net loss to the FY2024 consolidated figures [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 margins therefore blend ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of a loss-making acquiree (plus associated deal/integration costs), so its ranking is soft. Excluding Hawaiian's contribution, Alaska's implied standalone net margin is roughly $508M / $10,866M ≈ 4.7%, which would move it well clear of third place on net margin; an ex-Hawaiian operating margin cannot be computed because operating income for the acquiree is not separately disclosed [DOC-2].

## Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ revenue)

| Rank | Airline | Operating income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M | $61,643M [DOC-1] | 9.73% |
| 2 | United | $5,096M | $57,063M [DOC-1] | 8.93% |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M | $11,735M [DOC-1] | 4.86% |
| 4 | American | $2,614M | $54,211M [DOC-1] | 4.82% |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M | $27,483M [DOC-1] | 1.17% |

Alaska and American are effectively tied (4 bps apart), and that ordering is within the noise created by the Hawaiian consolidation.

## Net margin, FY2024 (net income ÷ revenue)

| Rank | Airline | Net income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $3,457M | $61,643M [DOC-1] | 5.61% |
| 2 | United | $3,149M | $57,063M [DOC-1] | 5.52% |
| 3 | Alaska | $395M | $11,735M [DOC-1] | 3.37% |
| 4 | Southwest | $465M | $27,483M [DOC-1] | 1.69% |
| 5 | American | $846M | $54,211M [DOC-1] | 1.56% |

Note the rank swap at the bottom: Southwest's net income ($465M) exceeds its operating income ($321M), implying net non-operating income [DOC-1], while American's net income ($846M) is far below its $2,614M operating income, consistent with heavy interest expense [DOC-1].

## Conclusion

Yes — **Delta ranks first on both measures** (9.73% operating margin, 5.61% net margin), with United a close second in each case. The rankings differ only in the lower half (Southwest and American swap 4th/5th).

ANSWER: Operating margin: Delta 9.73% > United 8.93% > Alaska 4.86% > American 4.82% > Southwest 1.17%. Net margin: Delta 5.61% > United 5.52% > Alaska 3.37% > Southwest 1.69% > American 1.56%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked in both (note: Alaska's figures include Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so Alaska is not fully comparable).
